slides.title: A holy man lived on top of a pillar for about 37 years.
Too extreme for the monks
slides.body: Simeon, a shepherd's son, joined a monastery as a youth. His austerities alarmed the community, and he was asked to leave.

slides.title: Up he went
slides.body: Near Aleppo, as crowds grew, he climbed a column, probably around 420. The first was perhaps 3 m high; the last, by most accounts, over 15 m.

slides.title: Life on top
slides.body: Disciples climbed a ladder to bring food. He stood, prayed, bowed and preached through Syrian summers and winters until he died in 459.

slides.title: Emperors asked his advice
slides.body: Pilgrims came from as far as Spain, Gaul and Britain. Emperor Theodosius II valued his counsel, and Simeon backed the Council of Chalcedon.

slides.title: Then they chipped it away
slides.body: Pilgrims chipped his column away for relics until only a stump remained. His imitator Daniel lasted about 33 years on pillars near Constantinople.

caption: He was asked to leave a monastery for being too extreme, so he climbed a pillar and stayed about 37 years. How long would you last?
